INTJ>INTJ.title: You think things through before you move.
INTJ>INTJ.body: You think things through alone and decide what's ahead before you act. Before you go out, you've looked up the train home and an alternate route in case of delays. In meetings, you sometimes know "This is where we'll get stuck" before anyone else notices. You have a hard time getting motivated by rules that have no clear reason.
INTJ>INTJ.body_s: You think things through alone and decide what's ahead before you act. Before you go out, you've looked up the train home and an alternate route in case of delays. In group discussions, you sometimes know "This is where we'll get stuck" before anyone else notices. You have a hard time getting motivated by rules that have no clear reason.
INTJ>INTJ.say: "Bottom line, I think that'll cause trouble later."
INTJ>INTJ.do: Before going out, you check even the train times for getting home.
INTJ>INTJ.worry: You tend to skip explanations, and people sometimes call you cold or hard to read. You do have things to say, but finding the right way to say them takes time.
INTJ>INTJ.karai: You see a new shop with a long line and think, "Will it last six months?"
INTJ>INTJ.aru: When a friend talks about their trip, you start reworking the schedule in your head. You asked, "Can you make that transfer?" and the room went a little quiet.
INTJ>INTJ.why: Both what you were born with and what you learned through experience are about building things out ahead, alone. Through all kinds of experiences, you've seen many times how thinking ahead would have saved you trouble. Because of that, you end up following even other people's plans far ahead. When you hear about someone's trip, your head starts calculating the transfer times on its own, so you end up saying out loud whatever caught your attention.
INTJ>INTJ.yure: You're likely to get nearly the same result every time you take the test. If a different type shows up, it may have been a stretch when you were leading people and matching everyone else's pace.
INTJ>INTJ.plus: You take time with words because you don't want to say things carelessly. Even if it comes a little late, what you say really helps.
INTJ>INTJ.tip: Before your conclusion, try adding, "Something's been on my mind." That alone helps what you want to say come across more softly.
INTJ>INTJ.hidden: You like things to go as planned, but you can also enjoy acting on a whim. It shows when you feel like dropping into a little shop you found by chance on a trip. Try it now and then, and the people with you will have fun too.

INTJ>INTP.title: Even after deciding, you can't help rethinking it.
INTJ>INTP.body: You like thinking things through alone, and you're curious about how things work. Even with steps you decided the night before, if you think in the morning "This way might be faster," you switch them right away. Even when things don't go well, you can switch gears: "Okay, another way then."
INTJ>INTP.say: "Hold on, I think there's a better way to do this."
INTJ>INTP.do: Once you know you're moving, you keep looking up shops in the new town.
INTJ>INTP.do_s: Once you know which school you're going to, you keep looking up shops in the new town.
INTJ>INTP.worry: You often think of a better idea right before the deadline. Before you hand it in, you want to check it "just one more time."
INTJ>INTP.aru: You plan your day off the night before, but on the day you think "this looks interesting too," wander off, and end up with a totally different day.
INTJ>INTP.why: By nature, you're the type who wants to decide on a plan and stick to it. Through experience, you started letting your thinking expand to follow whatever catches your interest in the moment. Making plans the night before is the habit you were born with, and wanting to change them on the day is your current habit. When something interesting shows up in front of you on the day, you want to check it out more than follow last night's plan, so the day turns out completely different.
INTJ>INTP.yure: Only one thing differs, "stick to the plan or go with the moment," so you may move back and forth between two types. On a question like "Do you plan things carefully?", your answer can split depending on whether you picture a work deadline or a day off.
INTJ>INTP.yure_s: Only one thing differs, "stick to the plan or go with the moment," so you may move back and forth between two types. On a question like "Do you plan things carefully?", your answer can split depending on whether you picture an assignment deadline or a day off.
INTJ>INTP.plus: You want to change plans because you notice other interesting things. Thanks to that, your ideas keep getting better.
INTJ>INTP.tip: On days off, try planning only the morning and leaving the afternoon open. Then, even if you wander, you won't feel down about "not sticking to the plan again."
INTJ>INTP.hidden: Your temperament also has the power to decide quickly. It shows when everyone is stuck choosing a restaurant and you say, "Let's go here." Use it at work too, and your ideas turn into real results more easily.
INTJ>INTP.hidden_s: Your temperament also has the power to decide quickly. It shows when everyone is stuck choosing a restaurant and you say, "Let's go here." Use it on assignments and group projects too, and your ideas turn into real results more easily.

INTJ>ENTJ.title: Somehow, you always end up running things.
INTJ>ENTJ.body: People around you may see you as a solid leader. But before the real thing, you usually take time to think alone. The night before a discussion, you write what you'll say and in what order in a notebook, so on the day you can move things along without hesitating. You're quick to turn what you're given into something real.
INTJ>ENTJ.say: "I've set the plan, so let's split up the roles."
INTJ>ENTJ.do: When planning a trip, the first thing you do is put places, times, and costs into a table.
INTJ>ENTJ.worry: After leading people, you feel worn out. The more people rely on you, the less time you have to think alone.
INTJ>ENTJ.karai: Halfway through a movie you know the ending, and you're holding back from saying it.
INTJ>ENTJ.aru: You naturally took charge at the meeting, but at home you don't want to talk to anyone and turn off your phone notifications.
INTJ>ENTJ.aru_s: You naturally took charge at the group project meeting, but at home you don't want to talk to anyone and turn off your phone notifications.
INTJ>ENTJ.why: By nature, you're the type who gets energy from time alone. Through experience, you became able to stand in front of people and get everyone moving. You picked up the skill of running things, but where you recharge is still time alone. You use up a lot of energy while running things in front of people, so at home you want to rest for a while without hearing anyone's voice.
INTJ>ENTJ.yure: The question that trips you up is "Do you get energy from being with people?" Picture yourself leading a team, and you'll lean toward the people side. Picture a day off, and you'll lean toward the alone side.
INTJ>ENTJ.plus: You're drained at night because you gave it your all in front of people during the day. Not many people can take what they thought up alone and make it happen with others.
INTJ>ENTJ.tip: After anything where you lead people, set aside 30 minutes when you don't talk to anyone. Zoning out alone on the way home counts as real rest too.
INTJ>ENTJ.hidden: Your temperament has the power to think things through alone. Have you ever thought about something important overnight without asking anyone, and that answer turned out best? When you're unsure, try taking some time alone first.

INTJ>ENTP.title: You come up with new ideas while chatting.
INTJ>ENTP.body: Something you said as a joke, you're seriously planning the next day. When a conversation with friends gets going, you throw out idea after idea on the spot, and on the way home you're already thinking about where to start. Talking with people makes your thinking spread out more and more.
INTJ>ENTP.say: "Nice. But in the long run, this one might be better."
INTJ>ENTP.do: You work out your own strategy for a favorite game and teach it to friends.
INTJ>ENTP.worry: The more excited everyone gets, the more ideas pile up, and the job of sorting them comes to you. Some weeks you want to keep adding ideas one day and narrow them down the next.
INTJ>ENTP.karai: Standing in line at a shop, you're thinking of ways they could move it faster.
INTJ>ENTP.aru: You got everyone excited with ideas while chatting, and then when it's time to decide, somehow you're the one organizing it all.
INTJ>ENTP.why: By nature, you're the type who thinks alone and wants to follow a plan. Through all kinds of experiences, you started expanding ideas while talking with people and changing things on the spot. Getting things going is your current way, and wanting to wrap things up is the way you were born with. It bothers you when a lot of ideas come up and nothing gets settled, so when it's time to decide, you end up taking on the role of pulling it together yourself.
INTJ>ENTP.yure: Your answers tend to wobble on two questions: "Do people give you energy?" and "Do you plan ahead?" It depends on whether you picture yourself chatting with friends or planning alone.
INTJ>ENTP.plus: The organizing comes to you because people trust you. They probably feel you'll make it happen.
INTJ>ENTP.tip: When an idea comes up while chatting, ask right then, "Who's doing this?" Once someone's in charge, it won't all land on you.
INTJ>ENTP.hidden: Your temperament has the power to really talk one-on-one. Has someone ever opened up to you about their worries when it was just the two of you walking home? Make time for slow talks with people you're close to.

INTJ>INFJ.title: You try to say even hard things kindly.
INTJ>INFJ.body: When you need to correct someone younger, you know right away what to say, but you spend days unsure how to say it. That's you. Even with messages, you reread them several times before sending and rephrase words that might sound harsh. You think carefully about how others feel, so people often come to you for advice.
INTJ>INFJ.say: "This is hard to say, but it matters, so I'll tell you now."
INTJ>INFJ.do: After a movie, you keep thinking about what the ending meant all the way home.
INTJ>INFJ.worry: Even when you think something is right, you hold back because you don't want to hurt anyone. You understand people's feelings, so you tend to carry their worries too.
INTJ>INFJ.karai: When planning your weekend, the first thing you book is a day with no one.
INTJ>INFJ.aru: A friend asked for advice, and you knew the answer right away. But you worried it might hurt, so you just sent, "Don't push yourself."
INTJ>INFJ.why: By nature, you're the type who decides with logic. As you've gotten older, you started making decisions that value people's feelings. You still reach answers just as fast, and now you take time with how to say them. Even with the right answer, you think it might be too heavy for the person right now, so you start with just "Don't push yourself too hard."
INTJ>INFJ.yure: The question that trips you up is whether you decide with logic or feelings. Picture yourself making a call at work, and you lean toward logic. Picture yourself talking with a friend, and you lean toward feelings.
INTJ>INFJ.yure_s: The question that trips you up is whether you decide with logic or feelings. Picture yourself making a call in your club or on a committee, and you lean toward logic. Picture yourself talking with a friend, and you lean toward feelings.
INTJ>INFJ.plus: You hold back because you truly care about the other person. Words from someone like that really reach people.
INTJ>INFJ.tip: When you give your opinion, try putting it as "I might do it this way." It won't sound pushy, and it's easier to hear.
INTJ>INFJ.hidden: Your temperament also has the power to see things fairly. It shows when friends argue and you can calmly listen to both sides. At work, people will rely on you as someone who stays clear-headed.
INTJ>INFJ.hidden_s: Your temperament also has the power to see things fairly. It shows when friends argue and you can calmly listen to both sides. In your club or class, people will rely on you as someone who stays clear-headed.

INTJ>INFP.title: Some days you know what to do, but your heart isn't in it.
INTJ>INFP.body: You like time alone, and you like thinking up new things. When it's something you love, you research it until midnight and fill your notebook with notes. But on days you're not feeling it, it's hard to get started.
INTJ>INFP.say: "I get the reason. But I want to think about it a bit more."
INTJ>INFP.do: Even with weekend plans set, you change where you go based on your mood that day.
INTJ>INFP.worry: Some days you know you should do it, but your feelings can't keep up. When your plans and your mood keep clashing, you get tired.
INTJ>INFP.karai: You start looking something up, and suddenly it's evening.
INTJ>INFP.aru: You decided to study for a certificate "30 minutes a day," but on days you're not feeling it, you just end up watching videos.
INTJ>INFP.aru_s: You decided to study Spanish "30 minutes a day," but on days you're not feeling it, you just end up watching videos.
INTJ>INFP.why: By nature, you're the type who thinks with logic and wants to follow a plan. Through experience, you came to value your own feelings and go with your mood that day. Making the schedule is the mind you were born with, and whether your hands actually move is decided by how you feel now. "30 minutes every day" is a plan your head made, but your mood decides whether you actually do it, so on days you're not feeling it, you end up just watching videos.
INTJ>INFP.yure: Two of the four sides are different, so your result changes easily. On "logic or feelings?" and "do you like sticking to plans?" your answer depends on whether you picture yourself at work or doing something you love.
INTJ>INFP.yure_s: Two of the four sides are different, so your result changes easily. On "logic or feelings?" and "do you like sticking to plans?" your answer depends on whether you picture yourself studying or doing something you love.
INTJ>INFP.plus: Your feelings lag because you want to put your heart into it. You can make plans too, so what you want to do will come true someday.
INTJ>INFP.tip: Instead of "this task on this day," try "any one of these this week." When you can pick by mood, it's easier to get going.
INTJ>INFP.hidden: Your temperament has the power to understand how things work, step by step. It shows when you pick up the rules of a new game or how to use a new gadget quickly. Use it, and you'll be able to explain your thoughts clearly to others.
INTJ>INFP.hidden_s: Your temperament has the power to understand how things work, step by step. It shows when you pick up the rules of a new game or how to use a new app quickly. Use it, and you'll be able to explain your thoughts clearly to others.

INTJ>ENFJ.title: Someone who cheers everyone on with a bright smile.
INTJ>ENFJ.body: In front of people, you cheer everyone on brightly. But on the way home, you're thinking alone about how to help everyone reach their goals. For each person you cheered on, you decide "Next I'll help with this," and you really do it.
INTJ>ENFJ.say: "You can do it! Let's get this far by next week."
INTJ>ENFJ.do: When a junior is feeling down, you work out a way of doing things that suits them, together.
INTJ>ENFJ.worry: Because you're good at encouraging others, you take things on with a smile even when you're worn down. When time with people keeps piling up, you don't get enough time alone to rest.
INTJ>ENFJ.karai: At year's end, nobody asked, but you're already thinking about dates for next year's get-togethers.
INTJ>ENFJ.aru: Even on tired days, when someone asks, you smile and say, "Leave it to me." Then at home, you collapse and don't talk to anyone.
INTJ>ENFJ.why: By nature, you're the type who thinks alone and decides with logic. Through all kinds of experiences, you came to connect with people and value their feelings. You've become able to move with energy in front of people, but the place you recharge is still time alone. When someone asks for help, not wanting to let them down lets you say "Leave it to me," but the energy you used doesn't come back until you're home alone.
INTJ>ENFJ.yure: Your answers tend to wobble on "Do people give you energy?" and "Logic or feelings?" The result depends on whether you picture yourself cheering people on or planning alone.
INTJ>ENFJ.plus: You say yes with a smile because you really want to live up to people's hopes. Now and then, give that kindness to yourself too.
INTJ>ENFJ.tip: In weeks full of plans with people, block out one empty day first. If the rest day is set first, you'll still have time alone to recover.
INTJ>ENFJ.hidden: Your temperament has the power to calmly find what's causing a problem. It shows when you're listening to a friend vent and think, "It's probably this." Gently share that along with your encouragement, and it'll be easier for them to act.

INTJ>ENFP.title: Ideas just keep coming to you.
INTJ>ENFP.body: You jump in right away, "Sounds fun, I'm in!", and later you also notice, "But I'm worried about this part." On the night you said yes to a spur-of-the-moment trip, you're alone looking up the weather and the time to head home. Some days you get excited with people, and some days you want to think alone, so the way you act changes depending on the moment.
INTJ>ENFP.say: "Don't you think we could make it even more fun?"
INTJ>ENFP.do: When a friend says they're starting something, you throw out idea after idea: "What if you tried this?"
INTJ>ENFP.worry: The gap between days you want people and days you want no one is wide, so planning your week is tricky. Judging your spur-of-the-moment choices harshly afterward can wear you out.
INTJ>ENFP.karai: You guess what happens next in a drama, and when you're right, you say, "Told you."
INTJ>ENFP.aru: You get excited talking about dreams with a friend, then at home you think, "Maybe it's not possible."
INTJ>ENFP.why: By nature, you're the type who thinks alone, decides with logic, and wants to follow a plan. Through experience, you came to get excited with people, value feelings, and go along with the moment. Three of the four letters are different, so the way you think changes a lot between being with people and being alone. With friends, your feelings make your dreams grow, and once you're alone, your step-by-step thinking comes back, so at home you end up thinking, "Maybe that's impossible."
INTJ>ENFP.yure: Three of your four sides differ, so your result can change a lot each time. Depending on whether you picture yourself joking around with friends or reviewing a plan alone, the result can look like a completely different type.
INTJ>ENFP.plus: You go back over your ideas because you really want to try them. The more you check them, the easier it is for your ideas to actually happen.
INTJ>ENFP.tip: On nights after a lot of excitement, save thinking about the plan's weak spots for the next morning. Tired nights pull your thoughts toward the worst, and mornings let you look again calmly.
INTJ>ENFP.hidden: Your temperament has the power to follow a plan to the end. It shows when, the day before a trip, you want to pack everything and get ready based on the departure time. Use it on things you want to do, and your ideas are more likely to become real.

INTJ>ISTJ.title: Even with new things, you look into them before you start.
INTJ>ISTJ.body: Even when you think of a new way to do something, you properly look into "How did it go before?" You ask people who did the same thing before, and note in advance where they stumbled. Thanks to that, you rarely make big mistakes.
INTJ>ISTJ.say: "If we're changing how we do it, let's look at last year's numbers first."
INTJ>ISTJ.say_s: "If we're changing how we do it, let's look at last year's records first."
INTJ>ISTJ.do: When you find waste in how work gets done, you first try changing just your own part.
INTJ>ISTJ.do_s: When you find waste in how your team practices, you first try changing just your own part.
INTJ>ISTJ.worry: Because you check carefully, it takes a while before you start on your ideas. You often get stuck between wanting to try and not wanting to fail.
INTJ>ISTJ.karai: You finish a task before the deadline and feel quietly pleased with yourself.
INTJ>ISTJ.karai_s: You finish an assignment before the deadline and feel quietly pleased with yourself.
INTJ>ISTJ.aru: Before buying a new appliance, you read and compare lots of reviews. In the end, you go with the same brand as before.
INTJ>ISTJ.aru_s: Before buying new earbuds, you read and compare lots of reviews. In the end, you go with the same brand as before.
INTJ>ISTJ.why: By nature, you're the type who imagines the future and thinks about it. Through experience, you started checking how things have been done and what people who actually used something say. You're still drawn to new things. As you compare lots of reviews, the fact that something worked fine before starts to feel like the surest thing, so in the end you pick the same brand.
INTJ>ISTJ.yure: Questions like "Do you trust new ideas or experience?" make you waver. Picture work where you can't make mistakes, and you lean toward experience. Picture thinking about your future, and you lean toward ideas.
INTJ>ISTJ.yure_s: Questions like "Do you trust new ideas or experience?" make you waver. Picture a test where you can't make mistakes, and you lean toward experience. Picture thinking about your future, and you lean toward ideas.
INTJ>ISTJ.plus: Even if it takes time, ideas you've checked first don't fall apart. People feel safe going along with your ideas.
INTJ>ISTJ.tip: When you research, set a limit first, like "20 reviews max." For new things, it also helps to try a small version once.
INTJ>ISTJ.hidden: Your temperament has the power to imagine things that don't exist yet. It shows when you're on a walk thinking, "It'd be nice to have a shop like this here." Speak up about your ideas at work, and you'll start getting new projects.
INTJ>ISTJ.hidden_s: Your temperament has the power to imagine things that don't exist yet. It shows when you're on a walk thinking, "It'd be nice to have a shop like this here." Speak up about your ideas in your club or class, and you'll start getting trusted with new things.

INTJ>ISFJ.title: You quietly get things ready before anyone's in trouble.
INTJ>ISFJ.body: Bringing an extra jacket, preparing spare handouts. Your thoughtfulness always comes a little early. On the day you go to a restaurant where someone once said "It's cold," you remember that and even bring a lap blanket.
INTJ>ISFJ.body_s: Bringing an extra jacket, having a spare pen ready. Your thoughtfulness always comes a little early. You remember a friend once said, "This classroom is cold," and on test days you bring extra hand warmers.
INTJ>ISFJ.do: The day before a trip, you put everything you're bringing by the front door.
INTJ>ISFJ.worry: Because you act before you're asked, people tend to take it for granted. While you're fitting in with others, your own time gets pushed back.
INTJ>ISFJ.karai: When someone invites you, the first thing you ask is, "What time does it end?"
INTJ>ISFJ.aru: You get ready for the get-together early and even remember what everyone likes and dislikes. When nobody notices on the day, you feel a little lonely.
INTJ>ISFJ.why: By nature, you're the type who thinks about what's ahead and decides with logic. Through all kinds of experiences, you came to remember past things well and value people's feelings. Your ability to prepare early is the same, and what you prepare is now aimed at each person. You prepared with each person in mind, so when nobody notices, those feelings have nowhere to go and you feel a little lonely.
INTJ>ISFJ.yure: Two sides are different, so your result changes easily. Your answers depend on whether you picture yourself planning at work or looking after family and friends.
INTJ>ISFJ.yure_s: Two sides are different, so your result changes easily. Your answers depend on whether you picture yourself planning for the school festival or your club, or looking after family and friends.
INTJ>ISFJ.plus: You feel lonely because you put so much care into other people. When you're around, people feel at ease.
INTJ>ISFJ.tip: Pick just one thing you prepared and say, "I got this ready." Often people just didn't notice, so one sentence will likely get you a "thank you."
INTJ>ISFJ.hidden: Your temperament has the power to think with logic without getting swept up in feelings. It shows when your family is torn over a big purchase and you calmly lay out the good and bad points. People will see you as kind and also reliable.

INTJ>ESTJ.title: You can get stalled work moving again.
INTJ>ESTJ.title_s: You can get stalled prep moving again.
INTJ>ESTJ.body: When work stalls, people somehow come to you. You hand things out in order, starting with what can be done with what's on hand: "First, this and this by today." You're good at thinking ahead and deciding the order of what needs doing.
INTJ>ESTJ.body_s: When prep for the school festival or club stalls, people somehow come to you. You hand things out in order, starting with what can be done with what's on hand: "First, this and this by today." You're good at thinking ahead and deciding the order of what needs doing.
INTJ>ESTJ.say: "Here's the goal. Let's finish these three this week."
INTJ>ESTJ.do: On family outings, you check when it's less crowded and set the departure time.
INTJ>ESTJ.worry: Because you can see the answer, some days it bugs you when others are slow. When you're leading people day after day, your time to think alone shrinks.
INTJ>ESTJ.karai: When someone asks for directions, you explain it carefully, down to how many turns.
INTJ>ESTJ.aru: At work you lead everyone, but after a day full of meetings, you just stare out the window on the way home without even looking at your phone.
INTJ>ESTJ.aru_s: In your club you lead everyone, but after a day full of meetings, you just stare out the window on the way home without even looking at your phone.
INTJ>ESTJ.why: By nature, you're the type who recharges by resting alone and imagines the future. Through experience, you started standing in front of people and moving things forward based on how they've been done before. You picked up the ability to lead, but where you recharge is still time alone. On days full of meetings, you've used up all your energy in front of people, so on the way home you want to zone out and rest your head without even looking at your phone.
INTJ>ESTJ.why_s: By nature, you're the type who recharges by resting alone and imagines the future. As you were given roles in clubs and class, you started standing in front of people and moving things forward based on how they've been done before. You picked up the ability to lead, but where you recharge is still time alone. On days full of club meetings, you've used up all your energy in front of people, so on the way home you want to zone out and rest your head without even looking at your phone.
INTJ>ESTJ.yure: Your answers can change on "Do people give you energy?" and "Do you trust facts or ideas?" The result depends on whether you picture yourself leading people at work or thinking alone.
INTJ>ESTJ.yure_s: Your answers can change on "Do people give you energy?" and "Do you trust facts or ideas?" The result depends on whether you picture yourself leading people in your club or class or thinking alone.
INTJ>ESTJ.plus: You get annoyed some days because you can already see the answer. Someone who can get stuck work moving again is relied on a lot at work.
INTJ>ESTJ.plus_s: You get annoyed some days because you can already see the answer. Someone who can get stuck prep moving again is relied on a lot in clubs and classes.
INTJ>ESTJ.tip: When you suggest a new way, start with "This will make this part easier." When people see it'll be easier, they're more open to change.
INTJ>ESTJ.hidden: Your temperament has the power to think years ahead. It shows when you see the news and think, "This could affect our work too." Say those thoughts out loud, and people will start asking you about future plans too.
INTJ>ESTJ.hidden_s: Your temperament has the power to think years ahead. It shows when you see the news and think, "This could affect my future plans too." Say those thoughts out loud, and people will start asking you about future plans too.

INTJ>ESFJ.title: You get the party prep going right away.
INTJ>ESFJ.body: When someone says "Let's get together," you're already thinking about seating and times in your head. You remember who left what uneaten last time, and quietly check before choosing a restaurant. Your get-togethers turn into ones everyone can enjoy.
INTJ>ESFJ.say: "I sent everyone the meeting time so no one gets mixed up on the day."
INTJ>ESFJ.do: You remember what's in the fridge and buy only what's missing.
INTJ>ESFJ.do_s: You remember what supplies your club has and buy only what's missing.
INTJ>ESFJ.worry: You enjoy doing things for people, but you notice you have almost no time alone. While going along with everyone, you miss your chance to say what you think.
INTJ>ESFJ.karai: On family trips, nobody asked, but you've already planned it hour by hour.
INTJ>ESFJ.aru: When picking a lunch spot, you ask what everyone likes and narrow it down. The place you wanted never comes up, and it's decided.
INTJ>ESFJ.why: By nature, you're the type who recharges by resting alone, imagines the future, and decides with logic. Through experience, you came to move among people, remember past things well, and value people's feelings. Three of the four letters are different, so you feel a big gap between the you who acts for others and the you who wants to think alone. Your attention goes to picking a place that will satisfy everyone, and you feel your own pick can wait, so things get decided without you ever mentioning it.
INTJ>ESFJ.yure: Three sides are different, so your result can change a lot. Depending on whether you picture yourself organizing a party or thinking alone at night, you might get a totally different type.
INTJ>ESFJ.plus: You ask what everyone wants first because you care about the group. Get-togethers with you there tend to feel comfortable.
INTJ>ESFJ.tip: Before asking everyone, try saying first, "I think this place would be good." If you say it first, you won't miss your chance.
INTJ>ESFJ.hidden: Your temperament has the power to see what's coming. It shows when you hear a friend's story and notice, "If this keeps up, it'll cause trouble later." Use it when you look after people, and you can help before trouble starts.

INTJ>ISTP.title: If you're curious, you try it yourself first.
INTJ>ISTP.body: When you've thought something through, you want to try it out first. You don't stop at thinking; you actually make it work. When you get something new, you poke around with it that same day and find the easiest way to use it.
INTJ>ISTP.say: "Let me try it. If it doesn't work, I'll try another way."
INTJ>ISTP.do: With a new recipe, you read it once, then change it your own way.
INTJ>ISTP.worry: Some stretches you want to plan far ahead, and some you only want to do what's in front of you, so it's hard to keep things steady. If you're not into it, you just can't get started.
INTJ>ISTP.karai: When you shop alone, you're back in 15 minutes, then notice what you forgot and head out again.
INTJ>ISTP.aru: With a new gadget, you just start pressing buttons to learn it. But for trips, you plan every detail weeks ahead.
INTJ>ISTP.aru_s: With a new app, you just start tapping around to learn it. But for trips, you plan every detail weeks ahead.
INTJ>ISTP.why: By nature, you're the type who thinks about what's ahead and wants to follow a plan. Through experience, you came to check things by touching what's in front of you and to adjust to the moment. Both ways are still clearly part of you now. Things you can try right away are faster to figure out by touching, and a trip you can't redo feels safer decided ahead of time, so you switch your approach depending on what it is.
INTJ>ISTP.yure: Are you picturing yourself working with your hands, or thinking about the future? That changes your answers to "Do you make plans?" and "Do you trust experience or ideas?"
INTJ>ISTP.plus: You test as you go, so your ideas really turn into something. You can also use what you learned right away next time.
INTJ>ISTP.tip: For big things, set only the goal and the date first, and decide the details as you go. Then you won't get as frustrated when plans change.
INTJ>ISTP.hidden: Your temperament has the power to imagine things that don't exist yet. It shows when you're fixing something and think, "This might be handier if I did it this way." Tell people your ideas, and they'll be glad for the new tricks.

INTJ>ISFP.title: You hold on to what you love.
INTJ>ISFP.body: You're good at thinking calmly. But you want your room to have only things you like. When shopping, you research the specs carefully, yet in the end you pick the one whose color or feel you like.
INTJ>ISFP.say: "Sorry, I'm going for a walk by myself today."
INTJ>ISFP.do: When buying an appliance, you compare the specs carefully, then pick by color in the end.
INTJ>ISFP.do_s: When buying earbuds, you compare the specs carefully, then pick by color in the end.
INTJ>ISFP.worry: When the choice that makes sense and the choice you like split, you feel a little uneasy either way. You find it hard to explain what you care about, so you go quiet when asked.
INTJ>ISFP.karai: After a big get-together, you breathe a sigh of relief once you're home alone.
INTJ>ISFP.aru: You had your room makeover all planned, then you found a vase at a shop and rethought everything around it. When asked why, all you can say is, "I just like it."
INTJ>ISFP.why: By nature, you're the type who thinks about what's ahead, decides with logic, and wants to follow a plan. Through all kinds of experiences, you came to notice the colors and textures in front of you and value your own feelings. Three of the four letters are different, so the answer your head gives and the answer your feelings give often split. Something you feel "I love this" about right in front of you moves you more than a plan you made in advance, so a single vase can make you rethink how your whole room is arranged.
INTJ>ISFP.yure: Three of the four sides are different, so your result can change a lot. Picture yourself planning at work, or relaxing on a day off surrounded by things you love, and your answers can be almost opposite.
INTJ>ISFP.yure_s: Three of the four sides are different, so your result can change a lot. Picture yourself planning out an assignment, or relaxing on a day off surrounded by things you love, and your answers can be almost opposite.
INTJ>ISFP.plus: You can choose by what you love in the end because you trust your own sense. Things you choose that way, you take care of for a long time.
INTJ>ISFP.tip: When someone asks why you care about something, try answering with a feeling: "Looking at it calms me down." When you talk about feelings, people just say, "Oh, I see."
INTJ>ISFP.hidden: Your temperament has the power to compare things calmly. It shows when a friend can't decide what to buy and you quickly list the good and bad points of each. Explain what you care about this way, and people will understand you more easily.

INTJ>ESTP.title: When someone invites you, you just go.
INTJ>ESTP.body: You look like you're acting on impulse, but in the back of your mind you're thinking about how to make it work. Even when you head out on a whim, you avoid crowded times and quickly check just the train home. Whether it's fun or work, being able to move fast on the spot is your strength.
INTJ>ESTP.body_s: You look like you're acting on impulse, but in the back of your mind you're thinking about how to make it work. Even when you head out on a whim, you avoid crowded times and quickly check just the train home. Whether it's fun or club activities, being able to move fast on the spot is your strength.
INTJ>ESTP.say: "If you can't decide, just get the cheaper one."
INTJ>ESTP.do: Watching a game, you explain which team will win and why.
INTJ>ESTP.worry: There's a big gap between days you want to be out and active and days you want to be alone with your thoughts, so you overbook and get tired. Later, you go over the things you decided on a whim.
INTJ>ESTP.karai: You read so many bad reviews that you close the page without buying anything.
INTJ>ESTP.aru: When friends invite you, you answer right away: "Let's just go!" The day after playing hard, you don't want to leave your room.
INTJ>ESTP.why: By nature, you're the type who thinks alone, looks at what's ahead, and wants to follow a plan. Through all kinds of experiences, you came to do things with people and enjoy what's in front of you. Three of the four letters are different, so the gap between days you go out and days you think hard gets big. When you're out with people, your current energy carries you, but you recharge in time alone, so the day after going all out, you don't want to leave your room.
INTJ>ESTP.yure: Three sides are different, so your result can change a lot. Picture yourself out with friends, and you get an active type. Picture yourself thinking about the future alone, and you get a totally different one.
INTJ>ESTP.plus: You can't move the next day because you enjoyed yourself to the fullest. Resting alone and then bouncing back to have fun again is a good thing about you.
INTJ>ESTP.tip: Before you answer an invite, take one look at your calendar. If you're already going out the day before, reply, "When's good next time?" so you don't wear yourself out.
INTJ>ESTP.hidden: Your temperament has the power to think far ahead. It shows when you're planning a fun day and think, "Next year we could do this too." Use it at work, and people will rely on you as someone who thinks ahead before acting.
INTJ>ESTP.hidden_s: Your temperament has the power to think far ahead. It shows when you're planning a fun day and think, "Next year we could do this too." Use it in your club or when thinking about your future, and people will rely on you as someone who thinks ahead before acting.

INTJ>ESFP.title: With everyone around, you look like you're having the most fun.
INTJ>ESFP.body: At lively gatherings, you're the one laughing the most. But you also watch closely whether everyone is having fun. If someone isn't part of the conversation, you casually turn the talk to them, and soon they're in the circle. When you get home, you quietly look back on the day alone.
INTJ>ESFP.say: "Today was so fun! When are we getting together next?"
INTJ>ESFP.do: You pick out the trip photos that same day and send them to everyone.
INTJ>ESFP.worry: The more fun the lively time is, the more time alone you need afterward. People see you as cheerful, so sometimes it's hard to share what you're really thinking about.
INTJ>ESFP.karai: You say "This is the last one" at karaoke, then sing two more.
INTJ>ESFP.aru: You laughed the whole time at the party, then on the way home you suddenly go quiet. You think, "I was really hyped today."
INTJ>ESFP.aru_s: You laughed the whole time at the class party, then on the way home you suddenly go quiet. You think, "I was really hyped today."
INTJ>ESFP.why: By nature, you're the type who thinks alone, looks at what's ahead, decides with logic, and follows the plan. Through experience, you came to get energy among people, enjoy the moment, and value people's feelings. All four letters are different, so the way you come across changes a lot depending on the situation. You may laugh brightly with everyone, but once you're alone, the habit you were born with of wanting to think quietly comes back, so on the way home you suddenly get quiet.
INTJ>ESFP.yure: All four sides are different, so your result can change completely each time. Answer picturing yourself having fun with everyone, or on a quiet walk home, and you could get opposite types.
INTJ>ESFP.plus: You go quiet on the way home because you put a lot of energy into having fun. Rest alone, and you'll be ready to enjoy the next time too.
INTJ>ESFP.tip: After a fun get-together, put some time to zone out alone on your schedule. Deep talks get through better one-on-one than in a big group.
INTJ>ESFP.hidden: Your temperament has the power to think ahead. Have you ever listened to a friend and thought, "If this keeps up, it'll be a problem later"? Gently tell them, and you'll become someone people count on when it matters.

INTP>INTJ.title: You follow your curiosity all the way to the end.
INTP>INTJ.body: You look into whatever catches your interest and turn it into something that actually helps people. You organize what you've found into tables and notes so you can show them right away when asked. You don't just leave what you've researched; you use it.
INTP>INTJ.say: "I want to look into why this happens."
INTP>INTJ.do: You look into why your phone bill is so high and switch to a cheaper plan that same week.
INTP>INTJ.worry: You want to think freely, and you also want to finish properly, so you're never sure where to stop. Even with a plan, when something new catches your interest, your mind drifts there.
INTP>INTJ.karai: You look up where a news story's numbers came from, and by the end you've forgotten what the story was about.
INTP>INTJ.aru: You made proper weekend plans, but you spent the morning looking something up and missed the time to leave.
INTP>INTJ.why: By nature, you're the type who lets your thinking expand to follow whatever catches your interest in the moment. Through experience, you started making plans and seeing them through. You picked up the ability to plan, but the urge to chase whatever catches your interest is the same as when you were born. When one thing catches your interest in the morning, your mind turns to looking it up instead of the schedule, so before you know it, it's past the time you meant to leave.
INTP>INTJ.yure: The only difference is "stick to plans or go with the moment," so you may go back and forth between two types. On "Do you follow plans?" your answer depends on whether you picture work with a deadline or a day off spent looking into things you like.
INTP>INTJ.yure_s: The only difference is "stick to plans or go with the moment," so you may go back and forth between two types. On "Do you follow plans?" your answer depends on whether you picture an assignment with a deadline or a day off spent looking into things you like.
INTP>INTJ.plus: You get so absorbed that plans vanish because you don't want to stop halfway. You can make plans too, so you can turn it into real results.
INTP>INTJ.tip: Before you start looking things up, set a one-hour timer on your phone. Just save the pages you're curious about, and pick them up on your next day off.
INTP>INTJ.hidden: Your temperament also has the power to adjust quickly when something unexpected happens. It shows when the train stops and you calmly enjoy finding another way. When trouble comes up at work, you can help others feel calm.
INTP>INTJ.hidden_s: Your temperament also has the power to adjust quickly when something unexpected happens. It shows when the train stops and you calmly enjoy finding another way. When trouble comes up at the school festival or in your club, you can help others feel calm.

INTP>INTP.title: When you wonder "why?", you have to look it up.
INTP>INTP.body: You look something up quickly before bed, and the sky outside is getting light. You've had nights like that. While you're looking things up, the next "Why?" comes up, and before you know it you're reading about something totally different from where you started. In places where you can think freely, you do really well. Following without being told why wears you out a little.
INTP>INTP.say: "Wait, why is it like that in the first place?"
INTP>INTP.do: When you buy an appliance, you read the whole manual before using it.
INTP>INTP.do_s: When you buy a new game console, you read the whole manual before using it.
INTP>INTP.worry: Thinking is so fun that you put off getting started. It may be all done in your head, but people sometimes think you're doing nothing.
INTP>INTP.karai: Your search history is all questions starting with "Why."
INTP>INTP.aru: You start looking up a word, and 30 minutes later you're reading the history of some unrelated country. Your family says, "You just lazed around all day."
INTP>INTP.why: Both what you were born with and what you learned through experience are about chasing what interests you, alone. As you've gotten older, you've had many experiences of finding something interesting on a side path rather than a set route. Because of that, when you're looking things up, you can't find a reason to stop. Your body may look like it's relaxing at home, but your mind spends the whole day chasing one "Why?" after another.
INTP>INTP.yure: You'll likely get the same type again and again. If a different result shows up, you may have been in a stretch of forcing yourself through deadlines or spending lots of time with people.
INTP>INTP.plus: Even when it looks like you're doing nothing, you're thinking the whole time. When the moment comes, those thoughts turn into something all at once.
INTP>INTP.tip: When your family says you lazed around, tell them one thing you looked up: "I'm really into this right now." Just a little sharing shows you weren't slacking off.
INTP>INTP.hidden: You're good at logic, and you also have the power to notice how people feel. It shows when a friend is down and you want to hand them their favorite snack without saying anything. Do that now and then, and people will feel at ease around you.

INTP>ENTJ.title: You take your ideas and try them out with everyone.
INTP>ENTJ.body: You gather people and actually try out what you thought of. The same day you say, "How about this?", you reach out to people who might help and even set the date for the first meeting. You don't let ideas stay ideas.
INTP>ENTJ.say: "I thought of a better way. Let's assign people and try it from next week."
INTP>ENTJ.do: When you find a handy trick in the software you use at work, you show the whole team.
INTP>ENTJ.do_s: When you find a handy trick in the app you use to make slides, you show your whole project group.
INTP>ENTJ.worry: When you're the organizer for too long, you lose time to think freely, and it feels suffocating. In a hurry to decide, you sometimes drop your own ideas halfway.
INTP>ENTJ.karai: You start explaining the board game rules before anyone asks.
INTP>ENTJ.aru: You said, "Let's figure it out together," and five minutes later you've decided it yourself and handed out roles.
INTP>ENTJ.why: By nature, you're the type who thinks alone and wants to move with the moment. Through all kinds of experiences, you started standing in front of people, setting plans, and moving them forward. You really do want to hear everyone's opinions, but the answer comes quickly in your head. When the path becomes clear halfway through a discussion, you feel it's faster to decide and act than to wait, so five minutes later you're handing out roles.
INTP>ENTJ.yure: Your answers wobble on "Do people give you energy?" and "Do you plan ahead?", so your result changes easily. It depends on whether you picture yourself organizing people or looking things up alone.
INTP>ENTJ.plus: You want to decide fast because you don't want to waste anyone's time. People who can really make ideas happen are counted on wherever they go.
INTP>ENTJ.tip: Even if you can see the answer, ask once, "Any other ideas?" When everyone gets to speak, they'll happily go along with the decision.
INTP>ENTJ.hidden: Your temperament has the power to change plans easily. It shows when the shop you planned to visit on a trip is closed and you say, "OK, let's go here instead," and have fun anyway. At work, it helps you handle sudden changes.
INTP>ENTJ.hidden_s: Your temperament has the power to change plans easily. It shows when the shop you planned to visit on a trip is closed and you say, "OK, let's go here instead," and have fun anyway. In your club or at the school festival, it helps you handle sudden changes.

INTP>ENTP.title: You want to share what you've been thinking about.
INTP>ENTP.body: Stories that start with "So I've been thinking about this..." usually run a little long. When you share an idea you thought up alone with a friend, one comment from them sparks an even better idea, and the conversation keeps growing. You take what you thought up alone and make it better by talking with people.
INTP>ENTP.say: "What do you think happens if we flip it?"
INTP>ENTP.do: When you get lost on a trip, you think, "This way looks shorter," and try your own route.
INTP>ENTP.worry: Talking is fun, but when you get home you suddenly feel drained and don't want to contact anyone. You get so many ideas that you move on before finishing.
INTP>ENTP.karai: With a new app, you skip the instructions and tap around, then go looking for them once you're stuck.
INTP>ENTP.aru: At the party you were the most into the "what if we opened a shop" talk, but when the group chat picks it up the next day, you can't reply until night.
INTP>ENTP.aru_s: Over food with friends, you were the most into the "what if we ran a booth at the school festival" talk, but when the group chat picks it up the next day, you can't reply until night.
INTP>ENTP.why: By nature, you're the type who gets energy from time alone. Through experience, you also started expanding ideas while talking with people. Talking is fun, but your energy still comes back when you're resting alone. You used up all your energy on the conversation the day before, so even when the follow-up messages come the next day, you can't bring yourself to reply until you've rested alone and recharged.
INTP>ENTP.yure: The question that trips you up is "Do you get energy from being with people?" Picture a long talk with friends, and you get the type that gets energy from people. Picture thinking alone late at night, and you get the type that recharges alone.
INTP>ENTP.plus: You're drained after talking because you were really thinking the whole time. Coming up with ideas with people and going deeper on your own is a good thing about you.
INTP>ENTP.tip: Don't try to do everything from an exciting talk on the same day; try just one thing the next week. On days you don't want to reply, a single "I'll reply tomorrow" sticker is enough.
INTP>ENTP.hidden: Your temperament has the power to dig deep into one thing on your own. It shows in the hobby you've kept up without telling anyone, which you somehow know a lot about now. At work, people will start saying, "For this, ask them."
INTP>ENTP.hidden_s: Your temperament has the power to dig deep into one thing on your own. It shows in the hobby you've kept up without telling anyone, which you somehow know a lot about now. In your club or class, people will start saying, "For this, ask them."

INTP>INFJ.title: After talking with you, people feel a little better.
INTP>INFJ.body: People who tell you their worries leave looking a little lighter after talking with you. That's because you calmly think about the cause and choose words that are easy for them to hear. You also don't forget to send a short "How's it going since then?" the day after.
INTP>INFJ.say: "No rush. Let's take our time and then decide."
INTP>INFJ.do: When you finish a book, you spend a while thinking about why it ended that way.
INTP>INFJ.worry: The more you think about how someone feels, the harder it gets to give your honest opinion. Your own worries, you tend to carry for a long time without an answer.
INTP>INFJ.karai: Walking alone, you get lost in thought and end up walking a whole train stop.
INTP>INFJ.aru: With a friend's problem, you can say right away, "Why not try this?" But your own worries, you keep to yourself for a long time.
INTP>INFJ.why: By nature, you're the type who thinks with logic and goes with the moment. Through experience, you came to value people's feelings and reach clear answers. Thinking things over alone hasn't changed, then or now. You can look at other people's worries calmly from a little distance, but you want to sort out your own worries alone before talking about them, so you end up carrying them a long time without telling anyone.
INTP>INFJ.yure: Your answers tend to wobble on "Feelings or logic?" and "Plan ahead or decide on the spot?" The result depends on whether you picture yourself helping someone or thinking alone.
INTP>INFJ.plus: Your own worries get pushed back because you've been helping others first. Your words really do reach people.
INTP>INFJ.tip: For your own worries, ask yourself, "What would I say if a friend had this problem?" You're quick with answers for others, so it'll be easier to find your own.
INTP>INFJ.hidden: Your temperament also has the power to wait and see without rushing to an answer. It shows when plans suddenly change and you think, "Well, this could be fun too." Use it, and you'll feel more relaxed with yourself and others.

INTP>INFP.title: You could talk about your favorite stories forever.
INTP>INFP.body: When the conversation turns to a work you love, both "This part is amazing" and "This part made me cry" come out. With a movie you love, you look up the meaning of the small details and then watch it again and cry. Your best side really shows when you're talking about what you love.
INTP>INFP.do: You watch the trailer for a movie you're excited about again and again, guessing what happens.
INTP>INFP.worry: You keep thinking about feelings that logic can't settle. Stuck between the right answer and the kind one, you're often slow to reply.
INTP>INFP.karai: When your favorite show comes up, you start talking fast, and regret it later.
INTP>INFP.aru: You replay a favorite song again and again, thinking about what the lyrics mean. But in the end, it's just "I like it because it makes me cry."
INTP>INFP.why: By nature, you're the type who thinks with logic. As you've gotten older, you came to value your own and other people's feelings. Your mind that thinks about meaning is the same, and now your feelings make the final call. However much you think about what the lyrics mean, what finally decides whether you love a song is whether it moved you, so you land on "I just love it because it makes me cry."
INTP>INFP.yure: The question about logic or feelings is where you waver. Picture yourself researching, and you lean toward logic. Picture yourself watching a favorite show, and you lean toward feelings.
INTP>INFP.plus: After all that thinking, "I love it" is what remains, because you love it that much, from the heart. Things you come to love that way, you'll treasure for a long time.
INTP>INFP.tip: When you talk about something you love, try asking the other person too, "What do you like about it?" The talk grows, and the people listening can enjoy it with you.
INTP>INFP.hidden: Your temperament has the power to sort things out in order. It shows when everyone wants different places for a trip and you listen, then say, "OK, so here." At work, people will see you as someone who explains things clearly.
INTP>INFP.hidden_s: Your temperament has the power to sort things out in order. It shows when everyone wants different places for a trip and you listen, then say, "OK, so here." In group presentations, people will see you as someone who explains things clearly.

INTP>ENFJ.title: You think it through before you cheer someone on.
INTP>ENFJ.body: When you encourage someone with "You've got this," you usually have a few reasons in mind. You think of three good things about the person ahead of time, and tell them cheerfully when you meet. Because your bright words have reasons behind them, the person can truly believe them.
INTP>ENFJ.say: "It's fine, you've got this. I have my reasons, too."
INTP>ENFJ.do: When a friend talks about a dream, you work out ways it could happen together, right then.
INTP>ENFJ.worry: Cheering people on is so fun that you tend to cut into your time alone. Wanting to meet their feelings and wanting to check what's right, you struggle to find words.
INTP>ENFJ.karai: When you cheer someone up, you end up listing about three reasons.
INTP>ENFJ.aru: The night before helping a junior with a problem, you think about their situation alone first. You cheered them on brightly on the day, but at home you keep wondering, "Was that the right way to say it?"
INTP>ENFJ.why: By nature, you're the type who thinks alone, decides with logic, and goes with the moment. Through experience, you came to get energy from connecting with people, value their feelings, and follow through on things. Three of the four letters are different, so you feel a big gap between being in front of people and being alone. In front of people, your attention is on lifting the other person up, so you only get to calmly look back on how you said things once you're alone.
INTP>ENFJ.yure: Three sides are different, so your result can change a lot. Answer picturing yourself cheering someone on, and you get a people type. Picture a night alone with your thoughts, and you get almost the opposite.
INTP>ENFJ.plus: You go over it again and again because you want to choose good words for them. When your encouragement has reasons behind it, people really believe it.
INTP>ENFJ.tip: If you're worried about how you said something, just send a message the next day: "Can I add a little to what I said yesterday?" Knowing you can fix it later, you won't have to stew on the way home.
INTP>ENFJ.hidden: Your temperament also has the power to enjoy the unplanned. It shows when the place you wanted is full and you say, "Let's try the one next door," and have fun. Use it, and you won't push so hard to be perfect, and being with people gets easier.

INTP>ENFP.title: New things to be curious about keep popping up.
INTP>ENFP.body: When you meet an interesting person or hear an interesting story, you immediately want to know more. When something catches your interest, you ask questions on the spot, and on the way home you're already looking up related books. You enjoy both talking with people and thinking alone.
INTP>ENFP.say: "That's so cool. How did you make it?"
INTP>ENFP.do: You try a dish you saw in a video, using whatever's at home even if you're missing ingredients.
INTP>ENFP.worry: Your interests keep moving, so things you start often stop halfway. On nights after a fun time with people, you don't get enough time alone and feel tired.
INTP>ENFP.karai: Your room is full of gear from hobbies you tried for a bit and quit.
INTP>ENFP.aru: At an event you've never been to, you start talking to the person next to you. Before you know it, you're asking all about their job.
INTP>ENFP.aru_s: At an event you've never been to, you start talking to the person next to you. Before you know it, you're asking all about their school and what they're into.
INTP>ENFP.why: By nature, you're the type who thinks alone and decides with logic. Through all kinds of experiences, you came to get energy from connecting with people and value their feelings. Your curiosity is the same now as it always was. When you get interested in the person in front of you, one question after another comes to mind, so you end up asking lots of questions even to people you've just met.
INTP>ENFP.yure: Are you picturing yourself having fun at an event, or looking things up alone at home? That changes your answers to "Do people give you energy?" and "Logic or feelings?"
INTP>ENFP.plus: Your questions don't stop when you talk with people because what people say is just so interesting to you. Even people you've just met often think, "I want to talk with them again."
INTP>ENFP.tip: On nights after seeing people, keep your schedule empty and spend time alone. Having time to slowly think back on what you heard helps you rest, and you won't forget the fun parts.
INTP>ENFP.hidden: Your temperament has the power to think things through with logic. It shows when you hear a rumor and notice right away, "That doesn't add up." Use it, and your easygoing side gets calm judgment too, and people at work will trust you.
INTP>ENFP.hidden_s: Your temperament has the power to think things through with logic. It shows when you hear a rumor and notice right away, "That doesn't add up." Use it, and your easygoing side gets calm judgment too, and people in your class and club will trust you.

INTP>ISTJ.title: When something goes wrong, you look for the cause first.
INTP>ISTJ.body: At work, people probably see you as serious and dependable. But in your head, "Why?" is always running. You follow the set steps properly, and later you look up the reasons so that once you're convinced, you can explain them to others.
INTP>ISTJ.body_s: At school, people probably see you as serious and dependable. But in your head, "Why?" is always running. You follow the set rules properly, and later you look up the reasons so that once you're convinced, you can explain them to your friends.
INTP>ISTJ.say: "I'll follow the rules. I'd just like to know why."
INTP>ISTJ.do: At a new job, you first learn the rules and try doing things exactly that way.
INTP>ISTJ.do_s: When you join a new club or team, you first learn the rules and try doing things exactly that way.
INTP>ISTJ.worry: You want to follow the rules, and you also want to think freely, so you often feel boxed in. You have so much to check that you miss the moment to share your ideas.
INTP>ISTJ.karai: You stayed quiet in the meeting, then on the way home you realize, "That plan had the steps backwards."
INTP>ISTJ.karai_s: You stayed quiet in the class discussion, then on the way home you realize, "That plan had the steps backwards."
INTP>ISTJ.aru: You finish your set tasks properly. But on your break, you quietly look up why the steps are done this way.
INTP>ISTJ.aru_s: You finish the set practice drills properly. But on your break, you quietly look up why the drills are done this way.
INTP>ISTJ.why: By nature, you're the type who imagines the future and goes with the moment. Through experience, you came to stick to set ways and do things properly. Moving your hands by the steps is your current way, and thinking "Why?" is the habit you were born with. You can follow the rules, but you can't settle down while the reason stays unclear, so you quietly look it up during your break.
INTP>ISTJ.yure: You waver on "Experience or ideas?" and "Do you like sticking to plans?", so your result changes easily. It depends on whether you picture yourself working by the book or looking up things you like on a day off.
INTP>ISTJ.yure_s: You waver on "Experience or ideas?" and "Do you like sticking to plans?", so your result changes easily. It depends on whether you picture yourself working through an assignment step by step or looking up things you like on a day off.
INTP>ISTJ.plus: You want to know the reason behind rules because you think about what they mean. You don't just follow them; you can also come up with ways to make them better.
INTP>ISTJ.tip: When you have a question about a process, don't ask on the spot; ask when work calms down. When people aren't busy, they'll really listen.
INTP>ISTJ.tip_s: When you have a question about how something's done, don't ask on the spot; ask when practice calms down. When people aren't busy, they'll really listen.
INTP>ISTJ.hidden: Your temperament also has the power to go with the moment. Have you ever had a day suddenly free up, gone out on a whim, and had a great time? Use it, and you can handle sudden changes at work calmly too.
INTP>ISTJ.hidden_s: Your temperament also has the power to go with the moment. Have you ever had a day suddenly free up, gone out on a whim, and had a great time? Use it, and you can handle sudden changes in your club or classes calmly too.

INTP>ISFJ.title: You quietly help out people who are tired.
INTP>ISFJ.body: When someone seems down, you notice first, think about why, and then quietly lend a hand. That's you. You might leave what a busy person needs next to them without saying a word. Your thoughtfulness is so natural that people sometimes don't even notice you helped.
INTP>ISFJ.say: "You haven't been sleeping, have you? Here, this tea helps."
INTP>ISFJ.do: You notice more energy drinks piling up on a coworker's desk and take one task off their hands.
INTP>ISFJ.do_s: You notice a friend has looked sleepy for days and take one of their class duties off their hands.
INTP>ISFJ.worry: When you're fitting in with others a lot, you lose time to think at your own pace and get tired. Even when logic says something's off, you hold back out of care for the other person.
INTP>ISFJ.karai: A weekend with nothing planned leaves you a little relieved.
INTP>ISFJ.aru: In a meeting you notice, "That explanation doesn't quite work," but you picture their disappointed face and can't say it.
INTP>ISFJ.aru_s: In a group project discussion you notice, "That explanation doesn't quite work," but you picture their disappointed face and can't say it.
INTP>ISFJ.why: By nature, you're the type who imagines the future, decides with logic, and wants to move at your own pace. Through experience, you came to notice small differences in front of you, value people's feelings, and support others steadily. Three of the four letters are different, so the gap between the you who goes along with people and the you who wants to think at your own pace gets big. Your eye for noticing what's off is the same as when you were born, but the other person's face when you say it comes to mind first, so you stop before saying it.
INTP>ISFJ.yure: Are you picturing yourself looking after people at work, or thinking about things you like alone? Three sides are different, so you can get quite different types depending on which you picture.
INTP>ISFJ.yure_s: Are you picturing yourself looking after people in class or in your club, or thinking about things you like alone? Three sides are different, so you can get quite different types depending on which you picture.
INTP>ISFJ.plus: You hold back your opinion because you care about the moment and the person. You can think with logic too, so people come to you when they're really in trouble.
INTP>ISFJ.tip: If you disagree, tell them one-on-one after the meeting: "About that earlier, I had one thought." That way you can say what you want without embarrassing them.
INTP>ISFJ.tip_s: If you disagree, tell them one-on-one after the discussion: "About that earlier, I had one thought." That way you can say what you want without embarrassing them.
INTP>ISFJ.hidden: Your temperament has the power to imagine things that don't exist yet. It shows when a casual chat makes you think, "Something like this would be handy." Share those ideas at work, and your thoughtfulness gets fresh ideas added to it.
INTP>ISFJ.hidden_s: Your temperament has the power to imagine things that don't exist yet. It shows when a casual chat makes you think, "Something like this would be handy." Share those ideas in class or in your club, and your thoughtfulness gets fresh ideas added to it.

INTP>ESTJ.title: You figure out the order that makes things easy for everyone.
INTP>ESTJ.body: You set up the rules at work so everyone can move more easily. But you yourself are already thinking about the next better way. The day after handing out the instructions, you're already writing "I want to change this part" on them.
INTP>ESTJ.body_s: You set up the club's rules so everyone can move more easily. But you yourself are already thinking about the next better way. The day after handing out the practice plan, you're already writing "I want to change this part" on it.
INTP>ESTJ.say: "If we do it in this order, we'll finish fastest."
INTP>ESTJ.do: When you're put in charge of a work dinner, you plan everything from RSVPs to the bill with no waste.
INTP>ESTJ.do_s: When you're put in charge of the class party, you plan everything from RSVPs to collecting money with no waste.
INTP>ESTJ.worry: When you're leading people for too long, you lose time to think freely and feel stifled. Some days, while explaining things to everyone, your own thoughts get muddled.
INTP>ESTJ.karai: While a friend is talking, you ask, "So which one is actually better?"
INTP>ESTJ.aru: You set a new way of doing things at work and got everyone to follow it. But you, the one who made it, feel the most boxed in by it.
INTP>ESTJ.aru_s: You set a new way of doing things in your club and got everyone to follow it. But you, the one who made it, feel the most boxed in by it.
INTP>ESTJ.why: By nature, you're the type who recharges by resting alone, imagines the future, and wants to move freely. Through experience, you came to stand in front of people and move things forward exactly as decided, based on how they've been done before. Three of the four letters are different, so the gap between the you who runs things and the you who wants to be free is big. You picked up the ability to make rules and get people to follow them, but you still want to move without being tied down by rules, so the way of doing things you set yourself feels the most confining to you.
INTP>ESTJ.yure: Three of the four sides are different, so your result can change a lot. Picture yourself leading people, and you get a type that sticks to the plan. Picture yourself thinking freely alone, and you get a totally different one.
INTP>ESTJ.plus: Because rules feel tight to you, you can think of better ways to do things. Each time you fix something, your workplace gets easier to work in.
INTP>ESTJ.plus_s: Because rules feel tight to you, you can think of better ways to do things. Each time you fix something, your club runs more smoothly.
INTP>ESTJ.tip: When you set a new way of doing things, say, "Let's try it for a month first." It's easier to change later, so you won't feel trapped by your own rules.
INTP>ESTJ.hidden: Your temperament has the power to notice how things work underneath. It shows when a random video gives you an idea for how to do your job. Use it, and you won't just keep work running; you'll create new ways of doing it.
INTP>ESTJ.hidden_s: Your temperament has the power to notice how things work underneath. It shows when a random video gives you an idea for how to run your club or how to study. Use it, and you won't just keep things running; you'll create new ways of doing them.

INTP>ESFJ.title: You listen to everyone and pull it all together.
INTP>ESFJ.body: To others, you look like a kind organizer who looks out for everyone. But in your head, you're always thinking, "Why does it work that way?" At get-togethers you even keep track of when to order more drinks, and on the way home, you're thinking alone about the parts of the conversation that bugged you.
INTP>ESFJ.say: "What matters most is that everyone has fun."
INTP>ESFJ.do: At get-togethers, you casually bring in people who haven't joined the conversation.
INTP>ESFJ.worry: You don't mind doing things for people, but when you lose time to think alone, you suddenly run out of room. Some days, after going along with everyone, you're not sure what you thought yourself.
INTP>ESFJ.karai: You can't say no to invitations, and suddenly your weekend is booked.
INTP>ESFJ.aru: At the reunion you smile and nod along. But in your head, you're noticing the parts of their story that don't add up.
INTP>ESFJ.aru_s: At class get-togethers you smile and nod along. But in your head, you're noticing the parts of their story that don't add up.
INTP>ESFJ.why: By nature, you're the type who recharges by resting alone, imagines the future, decides with logic, and moves freely. Through experience, you came to get energy among people, watch the things close to you, value people's feelings, and prepare properly. All four letters are different, so you come across quite differently with people and alone. Smiling and nodding along is your current thoughtfulness, and following the logic of what's said is a habit of the mind you were born with, so even while enjoying the conversation, you notice the parts that don't add up.
INTP>ESFJ.yure: All four sides are opposite, so your result can change a lot each time. Answer picturing yourself organizing a party, or looking things up alone at home, and you might get opposite types.
INTP>ESFJ.plus: You can set your own thoughts aside and go along with others because you care about the moment and their feelings. Not many people can bring others together and still think calmly.
INTP>ESFJ.tip: On nights after a day of going along with others, schedule some time alone to look up things you like. Knowing there's something fun waiting helps you keep smiling during the day.
INTP>ESFJ.hidden: Your temperament has the power to come up with new ideas. It shows when you want to say at the usual get-together, "Next time, why don't we try this?" Say it, and it becomes a get-together everyone looks forward to.

INTP>ISTP.title: You always want to know how things work.
INTP>ISTP.body: When you think "It's probably like this," you want to try it right away and check. You think, then try, then try, then think. Even when putting furniture together, you look at the instructions halfway, then figure out the rest while working with your hands.
INTP>ISTP.say: "I wonder how this thing actually works."
INTP>ISTP.do: When your bike acts up, you look up videos to see if you can fix it yourself before going to a shop.
INTP>ISTP.worry: You can focus really hard on things that interest you. But things that don't, you just can't get started on. Explaining your thoughts feels like a hassle, so people sometimes misunderstand you.
INTP>ISTP.karai: You grab the screwdriver before the manual, and end up with one screw left over.
INTP>ISTP.aru: You see how to do something in a video and try it yourself right away. If it doesn't work, you think about why and try again.
INTP>ISTP.why: By nature, you're the type who imagines the future and thinks about it. Through all kinds of experiences, you came to check things by actually touching them and seeing how it feels to do. Your mind that thinks about reasons and your habit of moving at your own pace are things you've always had. You know that trying with your hands tells you faster than thinking in your head, so you try a method you've seen right away, and if it doesn't work, you think about why and try again.
INTP>ISTP.yure: The question "Experience or ideas?" makes you waver. Picture yourself working on something, and you lean toward experience. Picture yourself lost in thought, and you lean toward ideas.
INTP>ISTP.plus: Your hands move before you explain because you trust what you've checked yourself. Answers you've tested really help.
INTP>ISTP.tip: When explaining feels like a hassle, just show a photo or video of what you did. It gets across faster than words, and there are fewer misunderstandings.
INTP>ISTP.hidden: Your temperament has the power to notice connections you can't see. It shows when you hear about something totally different and think, "This works the same way as that." At work, you'll be able to come up with fixes no one else thinks of.
INTP>ISTP.hidden_s: Your temperament has the power to notice connections you can't see. It shows when you hear about something totally different and think, "This works the same way as that." On assignments or in your club, you'll be able to come up with fixes no one else thinks of.

INTP>ISFP.title: Your "I just like it" has lots of reasons behind it.
INTP>ISFP.body: You say "I just like it," but there's actually a clear reason. With clothes you love, you know yourself what you like about the color or the fabric, and you notice right away when you see something similar. In front of things you love, you end up stopping for a long time.
INTP>ISFP.do: On days off, you make no plans and drop by your favorite shops depending on your mood.
INTP>ISFP.worry: Sometimes you want to think it through, and sometimes you just want to feel it, so some days you can't explain how you feel. When people rush you, your thoughts and feelings both freeze.
INTP>ISFP.karai: Everything in your room is something you agonized over before choosing.
INTP>ISFP.aru: You keep going to your favorite café, quietly watching how they make coffee and copying it at home. When someone asks why you like it there, all you can say is, "I just do."
INTP>ISFP.why: By nature, you're the type who imagines the future and decides with logic. Through experience, you came to notice the tastes and colors in front of you and value your own feelings. Your mind that thinks about why you like something is the same, and now your feelings decide first whether you like it. The liking comes first and the reasons only become clear little by little afterward, so when someone asks, all you can say in the moment is "I just do."
INTP>ISFP.yure: Are you picturing yourself lost in thought, or enjoying things you love? That changes your answers to "Logic or feelings?" and "Facts or ideas?"
INTP>ISFP.plus: You can't explain it well because you don't want to put your feelings into words carelessly. The things you choose that way make your days more enjoyable.
INTP>ISFP.tip: When someone rushes you, say first, "Let me think for a sec." Once you know they'll wait, you can answer without panicking.
INTP>ISFP.hidden: Your temperament has the power to imagine what could be. It shows when you look at things you love and think, "Putting this and this together might be even better." Use it, and your hobby might even turn into work.
INTP>ISFP.hidden_s: Your temperament has the power to imagine what could be. It shows when you look at things you love and think, "Putting this and this together might be even better." Use it, and your hobby might even lead to what you study or do in the future.

INTP>ESTP.title: You find the fastest way, right on the spot.
INTP>ESTP.body: When you think of something, you try it first, and if it doesn't work, you stop right away and rethink. People around you are often surprised at how fast you switch gears. When friends invite you, you head out right away, and even if something goes wrong where you end up, you find another way on the spot.
INTP>ESTP.say: "That road's jammed. Let's go around this way."
INTP>ESTP.do: When you start a new board game, by the third round you've already figured out how to win.
INTP>ESTP.worry: When you spend a long time doing things with people, you don't get enough time alone to sort out your thoughts. Some days, you second-guess things you decided on impulse.
INTP>ESTP.karai: You pick the checkout line that looks fastest, and the one next to it moves first.
INTP>ESTP.aru: You and your friends got excited and booked a trip on a whim, but alone at night you're rethinking it: "Was that really a good idea?"
INTP>ESTP.why: By nature, you're the type who recharges by resting alone and imagines the future. Through all kinds of experiences, you came to do things with people and learn quickly from what you try. With people you can act right away, and when you're alone, you want time to think. With friends, you can decide on momentum, but on a quiet night alone, you want to recheck what you decided from the beginning.
INTP>ESTP.yure: Your answers tend to wobble on "Do people give you energy?" and "Experience or ideas?" The result depends on whether you picture yourself out with friends or thinking alone at night.
INTP>ESTP.plus: You can have second thoughts because you really look back on what you did. That's why you can use even mistakes right away next time.
INTP>ESTP.tip: For things you decide on impulse, make a rule: "If it still bugs me after a night, I'll change it." That keeps you from overthinking. Put some time alone before and after days out with people.
INTP>ESTP.hidden: Your temperament has the power to read what's coming. It shows when you can somehow tell your opponent's next move in a game or sport. At work, your speed gets foresight added to it, and people will rely on you to plan the strategy.
INTP>ESTP.hidden_s: Your temperament has the power to read what's coming. It shows when you can somehow tell your opponent's next move in a game or sport. In your club or group projects, your speed gets foresight added to it, and people will rely on you to plan the strategy.

INTP>ESFP.title: You're quick to find something fun.
INTP>ESFP.body: Even while you're laughing and having a good time, you're thinking, "Why is this, anyway?" When you hear about something fun, you go that same day, and on the way home alone you think, "What was good about it?"
INTP>ESFP.say: "Since we're out anyway, let's hit one more place!"
INTP>ESFP.say_s: "Since we're out anyway, let's check out one more spot!"
INTP>ESFP.do: On a trip, when you find a festival that wasn't in the plan, you go check it out right away.
INTP>ESFP.worry: You need time with people and time to think alone, so you're never sure how to plan your week. After a lively time, you're sometimes confused by how suddenly you want quiet.
INTP>ESFP.karai: Your phone's photos are mostly food.
INTP>ESFP.aru: The more you let loose at karaoke, the quieter you get on the way home, lost in your own thoughts.
INTP>ESFP.why: By nature, you're the type who recharges by resting alone, imagines the future, and decides with logic. Through experience, you came to get energy from being with people, enjoy the moment, and value people's feelings. Three of the four letters are different, so the gap between the you who has fun and the you who thinks hard can confuse you. The more you enjoy yourself with people, the more energy you use, so the walk home alone becomes quiet time for thinking.
INTP>ESFP.yure: Answer picturing yourself having fun with friends, and you get a people type. Answer picturing yourself walking home alone, and you get a totally different one. Three sides are different, so your result can change a lot.
INTP>ESFP.plus: Those suddenly quiet nights are when you're going back over the fun. You can tell funny stories and talk about deep things too, so people often look forward to talking with you.
INTP>ESFP.tip: The day after a fun plan, keep some time free to think about things you like alone. Share what you thought about with a close friend, one-on-one.
INTP>ESFP.hidden: Your temperament has the power to think things through calmly. It shows when a friend is down after a mistake and, while comforting them, you notice, "Next time, changing this might help." Use it, and you'll be more than fun; you'll be someone people can turn to for advice.
